rationale: Retain actual offline SQLite/JSON recovery, real admission ownership, archival preservation and failure injection; no duplicate or assertion-free case found.

cases.title: refuses %s rollback without changing the database when a move journal is unresolved
cases.reason: Both retained-backup and latest-JSON rollback encounter a real unresolved project-move intent before touching the database or intent bytes.

cases.title: refuses %s recovery before any mutation when a runtime has already entered
cases.reason: An acquired runtime admission and real open database reject both recovery selectors before even taking a stopped-runtime census; exact live and backup bytes survive.

cases.title: exports the latest SQLite revision through CLI before handing authority to an older build
cases.reason: An older stale JSON mirror is replaced by independently seeded SQLite revision2 while the maintenance owner excludes admission; original files and the new export are preserved in the actual quarantine.

cases.title: preserves all prior exports before archival (failure: %s)
cases.reason: Both actual archive success and injected durable archive failure retain all five separately seeded prior export payloads at the appropriate locations.

cases.title: leaves canonical JSON and SQLite untouched when the latest export cannot be published
cases.reason: A directory collision prevents publication and the real recovery preserves canonical JSON, SQLite and the retained backup, creates no quarantine and releases admission.

cases.title: rejects fabricated or released maintenance before creating the latest export
cases.reason: Genuine ownership identity and lifetime are checked by passing cloned and released maintenance handles; neither creates an export or alters live state.

cases.title: refuses a latest JSON handoff from a %s database instead of selecting stale JSON
cases.reason: Missing, corrupt and newer-schema real databases each refuse handoff while the stale JSON, retained backup and before-image survive without an export/quarantine.

cases.title: blocks startup between the stopped census and restoration while preserving complete original and restored state
cases.reason: The actual stopped census runs under exclusive maintenance; both competing admissions fail, restored independent backup data and all original bytes survive, then admission succeeds.

cases.title: keeps startup blocked after failed durable publication and permits an explicit successful retry
cases.reason: Injected durable-rename failure leaves startup fail-closed on preserved recovery artifacts; restoring the publication operation permits an explicit real backup retry.

cases.title: rejects fabricated or released maintenance handles before replacing any database bytes
cases.reason: Copied and released owner handles cannot replace real database bytes in the public backup recovery path.

rationale: Retain actual main-to-storage recovery boundaries; isolate headless runtime admission, preserve all claimed recovery bytes, verify retained SQLite and restore per-case environment/exit/mocks.

cases.title: restores the selected export through the offline CLI command
cases.reason: Actual main parsing and recovery restore the selected independent export, remove the damaged database family and refresh the persisted HTTP1 marker before printing a receipt.

cases.title: adopts current JSON through CLI with an honest source description
cases.reason: The current JSON bytes become authoritative through actual main/handler delivery and the real human receipt identifies current JSON without inventing a revision.

cases.title: keeps current SQLite through CLI and rewrites the diverged JSON
cases.reason: Also reopen retained SQLite read-only and verify its independent seeded document, so exporting correct JSON and then deleting or corrupting SQLite cannot satisfy the claimed preservation.

cases.title: refuses to keep an unreadable SQLite and leaves JSON untouched
cases.reason: An unreadable real SQLite primary fails the actual command with nonzero exit and preserves both original JSON and damaged database bytes.

cases.title: rejects ambiguous recovery arguments: %s
cases.reason: All ten explicit ambiguous or valued boolean-selector combinations stop before a runtime census and retain the database.

cases.title: keeps profile-state recovery local when remote selection is configured
cases.reason: Restore all stubbed environment variables and the prior exit code after each invocation; reset status and constructor mocks before each case so remote defaults cannot leak into subsequent recovery controls.

cases.title: recovers an absent database and archives every export (legacy JSON present: %s)
cases.reason: Both absent-primary and absent-primary-plus-JSON paths restore the exact selected bytes and archive every independently seeded export while restoring startup settings.

cases.title: preserves all live recovery sources when archiving an export fails
cases.reason: Check every original byte of JSON, selected export, damaged primary and WAL after the forced archive failure, replacing existence-only checks for three sources.

cases.title: falls back to restored settings when refreshing the marker fails
cases.reason: A forced durable marker-write failure leaves the old marker invalidated and the actual restored JSON supplies the persisted startup setting.

cases.title: preserves SQLite authority when the old marker cannot be invalidated
cases.reason: A non-removable marker path rejects the actual transition, preserving SQLite authority, selected export and prior JSON with nonzero command exit.

cases.title: does not invalidate the active setting for an invalid recovery export
cases.reason: Invalid JSON rejects before invalidating a real active HTTP1 marker or removing the primary.

cases.title: rejects an explicit remote selector instead of silently ignoring it
cases.reason: An explicit remote selector reaches the actual local-command rejection message and leaves the damaged primary present.

cases.title: refuses rollback while runtime is reachable: %s
cases.reason: Make the runtime reachable while the desktop app is stopped, isolating headless-runtime rejection from the separately retained running-app guard. This catches removal of the reachable-runtime arm.

cases.title: lists SQLite backups alongside JSON exports without opening the damaged primary
cases.reason: Actual exports listing enumerates a real self-contained SQLite backup and JSON export while the damaged primary remains unopened and no runtime census is taken.

cases.title: restores SQLite backup authority with damaged database present=%s
cases.reason: Both damaged-present and missing primary paths restore independently created SQLite backup data including sealed and extension values, retain the backup and refresh the startup marker.

cases.title: rejects a backup belonging to another profile before invalidating the startup marker
cases.reason: A real backup stamped with another profile fails before altering the damaged primary or active startup marker.

cases.title: requires an unambiguous retained backup selection
cases.reason: A retained backup plus a conflicting revision is rejected by main argument parsing with exact selection error and original primary bytes.

cases.title: rejects escaping backup IDs without touching any recovery artifact
cases.reason: Compare every original recovery source byte after an escaping backup selector, extending the database-only check to JSON, selected export and WAL.

cases.title: refuses database backup restoration while the app is running
cases.reason: With runtime unreachable but the app running, backup recovery rejects through the independent app-running arm and preserves original primary bytes.
